source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 8 May 1924, p. 5 ("Belfast rural council: only five nominations for nine seats in Castlereagh")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: names and divisions read on the block image of the News-Letter's nomination list of 8 May 1924

note: Triennial election of the nine electoral divisions of Castlereagh rural district, one member each. Only five candidates were nominated on 7 May 1924 and were returned unopposed; the remaining four vacancies were to be filled later by co-option (Belfast News-Letter, 8 May 1924). At the first meeting of the new council (10 June 1924) the four vacancies were filled by co-option: J. H. Burke Murphy, J.P., Jno. B. M'Cormick, Thomas K. Moore and Hugh English were co-opted members (Belfast News-Letter, 11 June 1924, p. 5). Co-options, not elections; the paper does not name their divisions, so no contest is recorded (round 2, 7 Nov 2026). Sole nomination. Returned unopposed.
